regions.merged_text: God bless you . I hope you are well - you and yours. Though it is just striking 11 p.m. I want to at least start you a few words before re- tiring after this busy day, and in a way even for me eventful day. For yourself of course, and for every one whose privilege it has been to be in immediate touch with the Eucharistic Congress out there in the Philippines it has been no doubt more than eventful. However, we here get the announce- ments over the radeo about 8 a.m. in Detroit and heard the Holy Father's own voice and benediction. His conclusion with benediction seemed to be really: ". in Nomine Patris et Filii et Spiritus Sancti". I hope you may send us details worth while. The press here - even the Catholic part of it has been very tame so far about this great event. I hope to learn that it surpassed in solemnity and impressiveness even the grandeur, etc, of the Congress in Ireland, of which Cardinal Hayes is said to have remarked: "It surpassed the insurpassible". Having barely missed going to that great event I almost dreamed of my going this one in '37. Had it been closer to the time of your jubilee I would possibly have been sent. I have not been anxious, however, to under- take such an expensive and extraordinary trip, - unless of course some ad- ditional duty should waft me thither. That I was sent to help Father Mau- rice to celebrate, seemed quite appropriate at the time. Now it seems to have been fortunate. In fact I believe quite a few blessings came as a con- sequence to myself & more. I have a letter from a certain ascetic invalid, Mary Kerrman of St. Elizabeth Hospital, Elizabeth New Jersey, I want to in- close ... well, just as a sample. Asking for details about the great Congress, I hope you may not think of taking as a criterion the example of the present writer. I am sure you expected some report about our visit in New York last June. As a matter of fact I started more than once to give you a short summary of my ten-day di- version, on that occasion. Hoping that it may not be without interest, I'll try just briefly to give you an idea about the whole affair even though be- lated. Father M. Joachim seems to have spoken to Rev. Father Provincial about it some months before, and the latter told me it would be alright. I started off Wednesday evening June 3rd. The evening and night were ideal in sun-set and moon-light, we crossed the Niagara about 13 miles above the Falls but even at that the waters seemed to be swirling on to as if rushing to a tragedy. Though I slept very little I was not tired when the dawn re- vealed we were descending the Mchawk Valley stopping only once or twice
